Paragraph: He who is satisfied with gain which comes of its own accord, who is free from duality and does not envy, who is steady both in success and failure, is never entangled, although performing actions.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Susceptibility to envy, instability caused by dualities (pleasure/pain, success/failure), and anxiety over unpredictable outcomes.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna states: 'He who is satisfied with gain which comes of its own accord, who is free from duality and does not envy, who is steady both in success and failure, is never entangled, although performing actions.'
Outcome/Resolution: Equanimity in all circumstances frees the individual from psychological stress and action-based entanglement.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Emotional Stability: Maintaining an even keel through life's highs and lows
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Freedom from Envy: Eliminating social comparison and resentment toward others' success
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Acceptance of Uncontrolled Outcomes: Finding satisfaction in whatever comes naturally without desperate striving

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Dvandvatito (Transcending dualities like pleasure and pain)
Sama siddhav asiddhau ca (Equal/steady in both success and failure)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Tranquility amidst dualities and satisfaction with spontaneous gifts keeps the soul untainted by actions.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Developing resilience to life's dualities protects against envy and emotional exhaustion.
